3f8e2b7c-5a41-4d9e-b2c6-7e1f0a9d4c21.content: Give me the Q3 cash runway picture. Start with what we know for sure.

## What we know for sure

- Cash on hand: **$101,700** (operating account, reconciled this morning)
- Committed outflows next 30 days: **$19,100**
- Receivables outstanding: **$27,680** across 4 invoices

> Everything below this line is a model, not a measurement.
What is our monthly burn right now, trailing three months?
Trailing three-month burn is **$19,970 / month** (Jul $19.0k, Aug $21.8k, Sep $19.0k). August carried the drive replacements.
Break the burn down by category.

| Category | Monthly | Share |
|---|---|---|
| Payroll & contractors | $11,040 | 55% |
| Infrastructure & power | $3,700 | 19% |
| SaaS & subscriptions | $2,270 | 11% |
| Legal & filings | $1,570 | 8% |
| Everything else | $1,390 | 7% |
How much of that is the GPU power bill after the GPU server incident?
The power line moved from **$1,020** to **$1,790** a month once both GPUs were under load. The new one-GPU-at-a-time rule should pull that back toward **$1,280**.
If revenue stays flat, how many months of runway do we have?
Flat revenue: **5.1 months** of runway from today, assuming receivables collect on their current pattern.
And if the Northbridge Tax contract closes in November?
Northbridge Tax at the quoted retainer adds **$3,840 / month** from November, which stretches runway to **7.3 months**.
What assumptions are you making about collections?

Assumptions I am making:

1. Receivables collect at the trailing 60-day pattern (82% within 45 days)
2. No new hires
3. Power cost settles at the one-GPU number
4. No refunds

Change any of these and I will recompute.
Which receivables are more than 30 days out?
Over 30 days: **INV-0231** (Bluewater Labs, $6,720, 41 days) and **INV-0227** (Maple Tutoring rescue, $1,900, 34 days).

arguments.query: SELECT number, customer, amount, age_days FROM invoices WHERE age_days > 30

3f8e2b7c-5a41-4d9e-b2c6-7e1f0a9d4c21.content: Draft the collections nudge for the oldest one — just the body.
Hi — a quick note that INV-0231 for $6,720 is now 41 days outstanding. If it has already been scheduled, ignore me; if anything on the invoice is holding it up, tell me and I will fix it today.
Do we have any subscriptions we could cut this month?
Four candidates: the second search-API vendor ($290), a dormant design seat ($70), the duplicate monitoring plan ($60), and the unused cloud GPU hours reservation ($350).
Rank them by savings and by how much pain cancelling causes.

| Subscription | Savings / mo | Pain |
|---|---|---|
| Cloud GPU reservation | $350 | low |
| Second search API | $290 | medium (search is already degraded) |
| Design seat | $70 | none |
| Duplicate monitoring | $60 | none |
What does the S-corp election change about the cash picture?
The election itself does not change cash; it changes **when** cash leaves. Reasonable-salary payroll taxes become monthly, and the distribution side stops carrying SE tax.
Model the estimated tax payment for Q4.
Using the trailing-quarter net and the reasonable-salary split, the Q4 estimate lands at **$6,160**.
Compare that against what we set aside.
Set aside so far: **$4,160**. Shortfall **$2,000**.
Where does the shortfall come from?
The shortfall is entirely the August drive replacements — they were expensed, which lowered the Q3 estimate, and the set-aside was never trued up after.
Show me the three-scenario table: flat, +1 contract, +2 contracts.

| Scenario | Monthly net | Runway |
|---|---|---|
| Flat | -$19,970 | 5.1 mo |
| +1 contract (Northbridge Tax) | -$16,130 | 7.3 mo |
| +2 contracts (+ Harbor Health) | -$11,730 | 10.8 mo |
What is the break-even monthly revenue?
Break-even is **$19,970 / month** of collected revenue at the current burn, or **$17,860** with the four cuts above.
How confident are you in the GPU cost line?
Medium. The estimate is derived from the utility bill split by rack share, not from measured kWh. I can pull the meter readings.
Pull the actual kWh numbers if you can.

```sql
SELECT date_trunc('day', ts) AS day, round(sum(kwh), 1) AS kwh
FROM power_meter
WHERE circuit = 'rack-a' AND ts > now() - interval '30 days'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1;
```

Measured: **612 kWh** over 30 days on rack A, which is **$145** at the blended rate — far below the bill-split estimate.

arguments.query: SELECT day, kwh FROM power_meter_daily WHERE circuit = 'rack-a'

3f8e2b7c-5a41-4d9e-b2c6-7e1f0a9d4c21.content: Recompute the runway with the measured number instead of the estimate.
With the measured rack-A number the infrastructure line drops to **$2,960**, and flat-revenue runway becomes **5.3 months**.
What should go in the Friday brief to Sam?
Three things: the runway number with its assumptions, the receivables over 30 days, and the Q4 tax shortfall.
Write the one-paragraph summary.

Q3 close: cash $101.7k, burn $19.2k/mo measured, runway 5.3 months flat or 7.3 with Northbridge Tax. Two receivables over 30 days ($8.6k). Q4 estimated tax is $2,000 short of the set-aside after the August drives.
Add the two decisions that are actually his to make.

1. Whether to true-up the tax set-aside now or at the January payment.
2. Whether to cut the cloud GPU reservation given the one-GPU rule.
Is there anything in this review you are NOT sure about?
Yes. The collections pattern is from six invoices, which is a thin sample, and I have not seen the Northbridge Tax contract terms in writing.
Flag the single biggest risk to the runway number.
Collections. A single 60-day slip on Bluewater Labs moves runway by half a month.
What would you want to re-measure next week?
The rack-A meter against the utility bill for a full billing cycle, and the actual payroll-tax cadence once the election is filed.
Save the three-scenario table to memory under q3-runway.
Saved under `q3-runway` with the three scenarios and the assumptions list.
Remind me what we agreed about the Bluewater Labs deposit.
We agreed to hold the Bluewater Labs deposit in the operating account and not count it as revenue until the demo org is converted or returned.
Last thing: list the receipts you used, one line each.

- Operating account statement, reconciled 2026-10-24
- Invoices INV-0227 through INV-0234
- Power meter table, rack-a, last 30 days
- Trailing-quarter P&L from Accounting-Ops
- Subscription detector run, October
Thanks. Mark this review as complete.
Marked complete. The summary and the two decisions are in the Friday brief draft.
Actually one more — what changes if the power cap stays at 300 W?
At a 300 W cap the measured draw drops another ~18%, which is about **$25 / month** — immaterial to runway but worth having for the power-path task.

9a1b2c3d-4e5f-4a6b-8c7d-0e1f2a3b4c5d.content: Give me a rollback plan for the Email-Ops prod deploy if the checkout fails again.

## Rollback plan

1. `deploy.sh` must **stop** when the checkout fails — no partial image build.
2. Keep the previous image tagged `rollback-<date>`.
3. `docker compose --env-file .env.prod up -d email-ops@rollback`.
4. Verify an exact token in the served bundle, not just a 200.
About **40 seconds** on gpu-01 — the image is already local, so it is a container recreate, not a build.

e6f7a8b9-0c1d-4e2f-9a3b-4c5d6e7f8091.content: How many clips per hour is the footage index doing on the second GPU alone?
Trailing six hours: **184 clips / hour**, down from 310 when both GPUs were on it. ETA for the remaining 2,140 clips is **11.6 hours**.
Correlation is strong (r = 0.91): every 100 clips/hour costs about 95 W on the second GPU. The 300 W cap is what is setting the ceiling, not the model.
